nodes.label: ETYMOLOGY — why these names
nodes.what: Where the names come from. Pure exporter: 8 roads out, 0 in — and zero pollination FROM any library doc in any epoch. ARCS imports all its names (Greek, CCRU, materials science, Chinese) and has never yet coined-and-canonized a term from its own material into this family.

nodes.label: LIBRARY — where it is written
nodes.what: 17 documents, 64 roads out — and in-degree ZERO across every document. The library examines everything and is examined by nothing: the unexamined examiner, at family scale. Three canonical books (Canon v1.1/v2.0, Codex v8.5, Phenomenology) pollinate nothing at all.

invariants.note: Three grades of always-true, deliberately distinguished. TAUTOLOGY: true by construction within ARCS's own definitions — load-bearing, but carries no information about the world. CONSTITUTIONAL: normative invariant KEPT true by enforcement (could be violated; never has been; violation = constitutional breach). EMPIRICAL: has never been false across e1-e8 but is falsifiable — the only grade that constitutes evidence.

satoshi.note: The receipt is ARCS's satoshi: the smallest irreducible unit of recorded decision value. The structure is fractal-recursive — the same DEWY decomposition holds at every scale, and ARCS uses ARCS to build ARCS (this audit is itself a receipt about the receipt system).

proverbs.text: two unsequenced calls to action compete; number the steps or the visitor guesses which comes first.
name the mechanical task as mechanical, and spend no deliberation it does not deserve.
know your actual distribution model before you optimize the surface; a warm-referral artifact is not a cold funnel and must not be tuned like one.
when the form itself is the cognitive tax you promised to remove, the form is the bug.
goals do not hang from a single parent; one small aim serves many large ones, so the honest shape is a lattice, not a tree.
beneath the stated problem lies the core want; transmute the raw complaint into the truth it is actually reaching for.
a prompt to ask next and an answered question already logged are different artifacts. do not let one stand in for the other.
no source is trusted for being familiar. another agent's output, and even your own prior word, is input until verified.
keep parallel frames parallel. the same five lenses aimed at a commit and at a decision must not be merged; a commit is not a decision receipt.
the decision is not what to build. it is whether this will be built again.
a decision is a discharge: it fires when the potential peaks and the gap aligns, not when the clock says so.
a decision carries two numbers, the audited and the assessed. never let the second wear the first's clothes.
the isolation that actually holds is the one at the layer your queries pass through; everything the privileged path bypasses protects only strangers.
prefer the clean end-state over the workaround whose suffix leaks into all future code.
a dependency blocks only what truly depends on it. ship the independent parts now.
a finding is not closed because it is written down. it closes with a mechanism that prevents recurrence, or a dated waiver that owns the deferral.
judge a build by whether the second case would fork it or reuse it.
the flash is not the decision. the confirmed receipt is; a spark no one received went to ground.
ship changes that are independently deployable and individually falsifiable, so each one can teach you something alone.
keep the calibrating step as fuel, not a destination; put no extra stop between the question and the answer it feeds.
sealing everything is over-broad and throws away a real asset. split instead, so the value survives in the open and the secret survives in the dark.
a one-off earns no mold. promote on the second real case, not the first.
weigh a decision by whether it would survive its own recoil, not by how bright it looked when it fired.
use the fast tool to bootstrap and the tracked tool to live; one decision names both and the trigger that switches between them.
automation authority is a topology, not a tier. do not ask what level of automation is safe. ask at what boundary automation stops and human agency begins.
lock the minimum that every surface must share, and let each surface own whatever it needs above it.
an instrument panel makes the user assemble the data first. a navigator takes the raw signal and finds the structure. build the one the hardest cases need.
annotate the sealed record, never rewrite it; a decision gains meaning from what wraps it, not from tampering with the thing itself.
infer the structure from the trail already left behind; to declare it up front is to freeze a preference still taking form.
resolve the architecture forks before any code is laid; name the gates first, and every downstream build inherits a settled answer.
a public act is one-way, but the decisions beneath it stay two-way; make the irreversible claim while keeping the mechanism revisable.
build the instrument that will tell you whether a better signal helps before you build the better signal; precision you cannot measure is precision spent in the dark.
a record of a decision is not the decision remade. the instrument renders the terrain, it does not adjudicate it.
do not guess an unconfirmed distinction into a schema, because the schema outlives the guess. route it as a cheap question instead.
when a richer version arrives, extend the single source of truth rather than stand up a parallel one to move faster. the fork is a debt paid later with interest.
when the code and the promise diverge, bend the code to the promise. the promise is your position; the code is only how you hold it.
a stored belief is never just a claim. it carries its time, its scope, its warrant, its debts, and its dictionary. drop any one and the belief reads wrong later.
to share a thing without storing it, hand the whole payload in the part of the link the server never sees.
author the cheap primitive and derive the expensive view from it. one source of truth, and the rich picture is rendered, never separately maintained.
instance, then class: solve it once concretely, then cast the mold the second case asks for.
recipe, discharge, receipt: the instruction given, the arc across the gap, the record of what arrived. one decision, three moments.
an empty cell is not a failure. it is a stub: a place kept for a proverb not yet earned.
when a change falls short, do not just block it. report the score, the weakest lens, and the one or two edits that would clear the bar.
what you built twice by hand, you should have built once as a mold.
every decision leaves a coordinate. the receipt is where it stood, so the next one knows where it stands.
a filed decision that keeps its tildes can be trusted years later; one that hid them cannot.
route discipline is a real control only while the routes stay few enough to audit by hand.
a dependency that fails silently takes your value away without warning.
a bootstrap shortcut used past bootstrap stops being a shortcut and becomes permanent divergence.
match the control to the real attack surface; a policy guarding a door no one opens is theater.
a silent fallback that hands back the wrong type disables every check downstream of it, and nothing tells you.
convenience machinery that quietly defeats the optimizer trades a hidden build cost for a cosmetic gain.
an offer shown before sense-making finishes interrupts it, and you lose both the free flow and the sale.
a bottom-up order left ungoverned calcifies into the rigid hierarchy it meant to escape; the heavy edges only grow heavier until nothing can move.
find the true bottleneck before optimizing anything; a loop that closes half a percent of the time is not failing for want of a sharper signal.
egress is a control, not just ingress. read-only is not safe. every outbound channel is a way for stolen truth to leave.
the recurring failure is always the same: documentation ends the loop. a finding that terminates in a file with no gate will happen again.
gating a page hides the surface, not the source. the history stays cloneable long after the view is closed.
silent fork-drift is the slow ruin: three copies that no longer agree, and no one chose it.
an attractor that pulls too eagerly does not find the pattern. it manufactures one.
defense in depth is a maintenance cost you buy when the access paths multiply, not before.
the risk you reject an option for is the risk you inherit the day circumstance forces that option on you.
every accepted trade-off should carry the condition under which it expires.
accept duplication only while it stays visible and localized, and name the horizon at which you will pay it down.
options that look like rivals are often complementary; do not strawman the fallback you may have to promote.
name the exact boundary conditions. a trip signal you can name is one you can audit on its own.
fail fast at the bridge, not silently at the database. a missing field should raise where it crosses, not rot where it lands.
speak only when ruin, derailment, or a sharp swing in conviction fires; commentary that runs constantly is noise no one reads.
when nothing yet exists to challenge an early commitment, hold, do not infer; locking before the flow can test it is the very breach the discipline exists to prevent.
a generated id is not a secret; enforce the owner-plus-record key at the application layer and treat row-level rules as a backup, not the primary gate.
a message that reports success but never arrives is more dangerous than one that errors, because nothing tells you to go look.
a secret in git history is a rotation event, not a fix. treat it as disclosed the moment it lands.
a shared link is a debt to everyone who kept it. delete the record and you break their reference, not merely your own.
assume breach. the architecture's task is not to prevent every compromise but to bound what one compromise can reach.
a zero-margin operation is a design bug, not a test of nerve. add a checkpoint that proves nothing is lost before you delete.
a one-off packaged too early is speculative generality, the waste that hides as foresight.
rank a signal by how hard it resists refutation, not by how well it fits the story you already carry.
unlabeled non-gaap presented as gaap is what quietly rots a house.
weigh failure modes, not features. bounded, one-directional complexity beats an unbounded, silent failure every time.
name the falsifiable test and the number that would kill the idea before you begin; a hypothesis with no veto threshold cannot fail, and so can teach you nothing.
instrumentation turns a launch from an assertion into a measurable bet; ship the measuring apparatus with the claim, and pre-commit the signal that would prove you wrong.
rank the guarded things by blast radius. the key that bypasses every other guard is the one to rotate first.
refuse the fix that quietly reverses a promise you already published, even when it buys a stronger guarantee.
weigh the fork against the mold: copy-paste is cheap today and dear at the tenth spoon.
a finding held by one stream is a story. require a second stream to brace it before you stake anything on it.
the counter-forces are load-bearing members, not patches; remove one and the structure slumps into a squat, dark, solid mass.
the promotion compulsion is its own drift: packaging for the pleasure of packaging.
the same basin that condenses fuel condenses delusion. the only difference is the control rod.
a fix applied only to the live system is not finished; write it back into the baseline, or the next fresh start reopens the same wound.
a rotation cadence that no human owns will not happen. a control without an owner is decoration.
governance about governance feels like progress while being motion in place. judge it by whether the next person acts differently, not by how well it reads.
what is already cloned is already disclosed. a rewrite limits the future spread; it cannot un-ring a bell that has rung.
name in advance the evidence that would prove you wrong, and the date you will look for it. a choice with no falsifier cannot be corrected.
every drifted shape was a mold you refused to cut when the second case arrived.
what did not re-converge across the runs was never a bond. let it decay before it costs you.
a grid that comes back full is the tell of padding. the empty cells are the honesty.
the window to promote opens on the second use, not the first and not the tenth.
voltage without an aligned gap is only stored potential. read the gap before you read the charge.
a gap between dev and prod stays hidden until the crossing; put the gate at the crossing, not after it.
the window to change migration tools closes the moment production holds a real row; baseline the history before that, not after.
put the default denial in place before the first outsider arrives, not after the exposure teaches you why.
name the explicit count or condition that flips the decision, so the revisit is a trigger and not a someday.
surface the price only after the value has rendered; the moment clarity is earned is the safe condition to ask for more.
set a falsifiable threshold conservative enough to be observable even at low volume, or the signal you wait for will only ever be noise.
a gate that clears on a count alone has not cleared; run the measurement the gate actually asks for before you walk through it.
place the only friction exactly where intent runs highest, at the moment of saving or sharing, never as a wall in front of the core value.
when unsure whether a safeguard applies, apply it. over-caution costs minutes; the skipped check fails in silence.
age every open finding against a clock. a deadline turns an unknown-unknown into something someone must act on the day it is filed.
ship it small, additive, and reversible, then let a few real uses decide whether it earns its keep.
do not cast the mold while the shape is still moving. wait for the second case to name it.
do not fire early. a discharge across the wrong gap is a short, and a short burns the circuit it meant to serve.
one access path needs one gate; a second enforcement layer earns its keep only when the surface outgrows what review can audit.
audit every caller before you delete; the grep that proves zero callers is cheaper than the break that proves one.
sequence the sure gains first and defer the aesthetic rebuild until the data earns it; the correct third move is wrong as the first.
the slowdown at the gate is not overhead. it is the integrity check the product exists to teach.
a synthetic test can prove the structure bears load and map where it breaks, yet it cannot set the operating point; only measured load can do that.
advance only when a set share of the gates pass; short of that, shelve gracefully rather than push a thing the signal did not earn.
a change that is additive, defaulted off, and reversible can ship even while the model behind it is still unsettled.
keep by default to protect what others rely on, but yield the moment someone asks you to erase their own trace. retention is a courtesy, not a refusal.
do not name a problem you cannot enforce. without a distinct mechanism and a reader that applies it, a category is decoration, not defense.
scoring a change that carries no judgment is false precision. rate what encodes a decision, skip the chore, and say plainly which it was.
order the work so the reversible, verifiable steps come first and the one-way gate comes last.
rule of three is the ceiling, not the target: promote at two when the second is already in hand.
the safe condition to proceed is a gap aligned and a potential peaked. absent either, hold.
a named gate turns an accepted risk into a scheduled action; without the gate, acceptable-for-now quietly becomes permanent.
when a thing waits on content that may never come, give it a deadline and a placeholder, so the wait cannot quietly become forever.
place the gate where the value has been proven, not at the door. a wall before the first taste kills the appetite it means to guard.
an owed action decays unread until someone closes it out loud. closure is a written event, never silence.
promote too early and you abstract before you understand; too late and every case is a fork.
timing is a position, not a schedule. the window opens where the conditions meet, and closes when they part.
never edit a locked schema in place. when it must grow, cut a version two and leave the first untouched.
recency and position are not authority. a point-in-time record becomes dead state wearing a live face the moment work continues past it.
the moment to cut the mold was the moment the copy-paste began.
mark where the arc struck and where it refused. the record of struck gaps is the map of when to move.
strip the formwork only after the concrete sets. pull it while curing and the structure falls.
an ambiguous name resolves to whichever match comes first, never to the one you meant.
a named gap is honest; a hidden one is a lie. when you cannot check the box, state the residual risk out loud.
never consume a claim that has lost a coordinate. trust it only to the fidelity it can still prove.
do not score a continuous gradient over input that is only qualitative. precision the data cannot support is a lie dressed as rigor.
a class is only as clear as its contract: deps, args, params, resources, schema, the manifest.
amplify the signal, never the noise, and never past the evidence that carried it in.
before you trust a number, look for its tilde or its custody; a value with neither is not yet real.
an unmeasurable claim is noise; one specific believable claim outweighs an impressive vague one.
better too specific for the few who lean in than too generic for the many who leave.
presence is not correctness; verify the value, not merely that a value is there.
canonical without enforcement is only a wish. two schemas will drift unless one source validates them both.
when conviction is still shifting, decide the direction but hold the build. a yellow gate is not a green one.

copy that could describe any tool answers no one who asked what this is.

coherence is a basin deep enough to hold, not an agreement loud enough to drown the dissent.

cryptography can prove who, what, and unaltered. it cannot prove harmless. authenticate the actor, then still question the payload.

a schema is how tools validate each other instead of drifting apart.

the mold that made the tenth spoon identical to the first was the contract, not the care that night.

local velocity compounds every day; zero-config is a feature, not a compromise.

the page's real job may be credibility rather than conversion; the private conversation is where the deal actually closes.

the mold is the leverage: cut it once, and every casting after comes nearly free.

the mold pays for itself on the second casting and profits on every one after.

a decision is a position under pressure, not an event on a timeline.
busy is magnitude without a bearing.

the first judgment ego clouds is your read of whether another's is clouded.
do not build tools. build the thing that casts them.
the recipe and the receipt are one word: the instruction you take, and the record of what you received.
an echo is signal only if it was independent before it was linked.
three axes bracing one point make a structure. one axis makes a story.
the leap is the fuel. the landing is the discipline.
reflexiveness is prepaid. it is never free.

sections.body:
ARCS is a reasoning instrument. It takes the decision you're carrying — the real fork, not the noise around it — and makes its shape visible. It stress-tests the question, surfaces what you might be missing, and produces a single clear direction graded by honest confidence.

ARCS does not make decisions. You do. ARCS never compresses, replaces, or overrules your judgment — it scaffolds and sharpens it. This is not a design aspiration; it is a hard constitutional rule of the system (ROM Primitive 1: NOTOMATION).

---

Using ARCS is not a subscription to a black box. It is a relationship with a transparent instrument. This document defines what that relationship is, in plain terms.

---

sections.h: 1. What is stored, and what isn't
sections.body:
**Your question (compass input):**
Processed in real time and used to generate your result. If you are not signed in, it is not stored beyond your session — it exists only long enough to produce the receipt.

**Your receipt:**
If you are signed in, your decision receipt is stored in your account and accessible via your history. It is yours. If you are not signed in, the receipt is generated and displayed in your browser only — nothing is written server-side. If you want to keep an anonymous bearing, you can sign in and save it; the write happens only after you authenticate.

**Sharing an anonymous bearing:** If you create a one-time share link for an anonymous bearing, the bearing is encoded inside the link itself — in the URL fragment, which browsers never transmit to a server. Nothing is written server-side; the content travels only in the link you send. The link renders once on the recipient's device (a per-device flag then flips it to a sign-in page), and because the content rides in the link, anyone you send it to can read it — treat it like any message. See ADR-037.

> **Disclosure (2026-07-13 — repair seam, kept visible on purpose):** From launch until
> 2026-07-13, a defect stored anonymous receipts server-side, contrary to this section —
> 48 such receipts existed when it was found. The write path was fixed the same day
> (commit `8b486e8`; the repository is public, so this is verifiable, not just claimed).
> The pre-fix receipts were deliberately retained rather than deleted: receipt links are
> made to be shared, and some are referenced in the wild — deleting them would break
> those references. They carry no account identity. If you ran an anonymous session
> before 2026-07-13: signing in from the same browser claims your receipts automatically,
> and a deletion request (via the inquiry link on arcs.care) will be honored.

**Your debrief:**
If you log an outcome (how the decision went), that is stored in your account linked to the receipt. This data is used to improve ARCS's ability to read terrain accurately over time — specifically, to validate whether the system's confidence grades correspond to real outcomes. It is never shared or sold.

**System logs:**
Standard infrastructure logs (request metadata, error traces) are retained for debugging. They do not contain your decision content.

---

sections.h: 2. Does ARCS train on your input?
sections.body:
**No.**

ARCS uses the Anthropic API (Claude) to process your question. Anthropic's API terms prohibit using API inputs to train foundation models without explicit consent. Your compass inputs do not train Claude or any other model.

ARCS's own modeling work (operator scoring, NCI calibration) uses aggregate, anonymized outcome data — not your raw decision content.

---

**Export:** Receipts and briefs are viewable and shareable via direct link. Full data export (all receipts, outcomes, and session history in structured format) is on the near-term roadmap and not yet shipped.

**Delete:** You can request deletion of your account and all associated data by emailing [contact]. Account deletion removes all receipts, outcomes, and personal data from the production database within 30 days. This is a one-way gate — deleted data cannot be recovered.

*These are commitments, not aspirations. When export ships, this document will be updated with the exact path.*

---

**Yes — partially, today. More fully, soon.**

The arcs-v9 repository is public: [github.com/flashesofbrilliance/arcs-v9](https://github.com/flashesofbrilliance/arcs-v9). The full application stack (Next.js, Prisma, the L0–L5 pipeline, operator logic) is inspectable and forkable. You can read exactly how your question is processed.

Running it locally requires an Anthropic API key, a Supabase instance, and environment setup — there is no one-click local build yet. A packaged local-first version is a stated product direction. It is not yet shipped.

The honest answer is: today, using arcs.care means trusting the hosted infrastructure. The code is open so you can verify what it does. The roadmap points toward self-hostable. If that gap is a dealbreaker right now, that's a fair call — and the repository is there if you want to run your own version in the meantime.

---

sections.h: 5. What ARCS is and isn't designed for
sections.body:
**Designed for:**
- Decisions with a real fork — where two or more paths are genuinely available and the choice has material consequences
- High-stakes clarity under time pressure — when you need structure, not more information
- Stress-testing your own instinct — when you suspect you might be thinking about the problem the wrong way
- Founder and operator decisions: capital, team, strategy, timing, partnerships, exits
- Personal high-stakes decisions where you'd normally pay for an advisor or trusted thinking partner

**Not designed for:**
- Decisions that are already made — ARCS is not a rationalization engine
- Pure information lookup — use a search engine
- Decisions requiring licensed professional advice (legal, medical, financial) — ARCS can help you think, not practice law or medicine
- Decisions with no real fork — if there's only one live option, ARCS will surface that, but it won't invent alternatives
- Passive consumption — ARCS requires you to name the real decision; vague inputs produce vague outputs

---

sections.h: 6. How much confidence should you place in the output?
sections.body:
**Honest answer: calibrated skepticism, not deference.**

ARCS produces a direction and a conviction grade. The conviction grade is the important part — it tells you how much weight to put on the direction.

What the grades mean in plain terms:

| Grade | What it means | How to use it |
|---|---|---|
| High conviction (GREEN) | The terrain supports a clear direction; the case for it is significantly stronger than the case against | Move. The system is confident and the Loki test didn't break it. |
| Medium conviction (YELLOW) | Real signal, genuine uncertainty — both directions have live cases | Use as one strong input, not a final answer. Cross-check with someone who knows the terrain. |
| Low conviction / contested (SCRATCH/FORK) | The question doesn't have a dominant answer yet — the fork is real | Don't decide yet. ARCS is surfacing the shape of the uncertainty, not dodging the question. |
| PARADOX | The options are genuinely non-separable right now | The decision is premature. Something upstream needs to resolve first. |

**What ARCS cannot do:** It cannot know things you haven't told it. It doesn't have context about your relationships, your risk tolerance, your financial position, or the hundred texture details that live in your head. The output is only as good as the input — and even a perfect input produces a direction, not a guarantee.

**The NCI score (conviction index):** This is a numerical grade of the decision's coherence and the confidence level the pipeline reached. It is currently calibrated against a proxy signal (stakes + horizon) rather than validated outcome data. Treat it as a soft signal — directionally useful, not mathematically precise. We are building the outcome dataset to validate and improve it. When that validation is complete, this section will be updated.

---

ARCS is built on a single constitutional rule: the system may only scaffold and sequence your cognition. It may never compress it, replace it, or overrule it.

This means:
- ARCS will surface the strongest case against your instinct (Loki test) — not to talk you out of it, but so you've stress-tested it yourself
- ARCS will tell you when the terrain is unclear rather than manufacturing false confidence
- ARCS will produce one direction, not a menu of options to defer to — because the point is earned clarity, not paralysis by analysis
- The receipt is yours — it documents the reasoning, not just the conclusion, so you can inspect and disagree with it

The goal is not that you trust ARCS. The goal is that you trust your own judgment more, because you've run it through a rigorous instrument.

---

sections.h: 8. How ARCS catches you at the fork
sections.body:
**Honest answer: it doesn't, yet — you have to recognize it and bring it.**

§5 above defines what kinds of decisions ARCS is designed for. It does not address a different question: how do you know you're standing at one of those forks *before* you ever open the compass? Today, the answer is that ARCS does not proactively detect this. There is no background system watching your calendar, your messages, or your behavior for a decision forming and tapping you on the shoulder. You have to notice the fork yourself and bring it to the instrument.

This is a real limitation, not a hidden one. Two things are true at once:

- **It's partly a deliberate boundary, not just a gap.** A system that silently watches your data for "decision-shaped moments" and surfaces itself uninvited is closer to the black box ARCS is explicitly trying not to be (see §7). Discovery without consent is its own trust problem — solving "how do you find the fork" by adding ambient surveillance would trade one trust gap for a worse one.
- **It's also genuinely unbuilt, not fully resolved by that boundary.** A consent-based version of fork-detection — something that helps you notice a decision is forming from signals you've explicitly opted into, rather than ambient monitoring — is a real, not-yet-built direction (`Kairos detection`, tracked as backlog in this repo's `AGENTS.md`, gated behind having enough real outcome data to calibrate it responsibly). It is not shipped. This document will be updated when that changes.

**What exists today instead:** product copy is the current, honest mechanism — surfaces like the homepage's "name the real fork" framing exist to prompt *you* to recognize the moment, not to detect it for you. That's a discovery aid, not a disclosure claim, and it lives in product copy rather than this contract for that reason: it's a UX nudge, not a guarantee about what the system does on your behalf.

---

> An associative index, not a flat record. *Shared documentation is not shared understanding;

> independently dated and attestable, which is what keeps it a self-portrait and not a story.

**Thesis (ADR-071):** Receipt and Induction are not two sides of a ribbon; they are two
traversals of **one non-orientable surface** — which is why the ARCS mark is a Möbius. Its
minimum stable cross-section is a **triad, none-may-null** (flagged verbatim in the Book of ARCS,
Nov 2025). It is held at the bottom of a **potential well** by the corpus's own accumulated mass.
Möbius = topology · triad = invariant · gravity = dynamics. One object.

---

## The induction circuit, named across 28 years

The Möbius is a wiring diagram of the author, named terminal-by-terminal in the correct physics
order (Faraday: `EMF = −dΦ/dt` — a changing flux *induces* a current; abduction *is* induction).

| ~year | self-naming | terminal | physics |
|---|---|---|---|
| ~1998–2006 | *the flux* (music artist name) | field / source | the changing Φ |

| 2026 | *ARCS* + the Möbius mark | the loop | the lossless non-orientable conductor |

**Self-exciting close:** the terminal phase is the **superionic nucleus** (rigid lattice + fluid
charge, one volume, conductive *because* fused). In planetary cores the superionic dynamo
*generates* the field — so the end terminal regenerates the source. A Möbius in time as well as
space: flux → current → spark → loop → superionic dynamo → flux.

**Torque and drive:** posterior reasoning → dynamo → **drive** (the current, from the settled
past); anterior reasoning → collider → **torque** (the half-twist, from the forward abductive
collision). They meet at a **spline knot**, resolved by the one *shipped* operator here:
**Operator21** (`operators/arcs_operator21.py`, P1 determinism PASS 2026-08-28).
